L29: # Devoted to the Fight Against Canine Cancer
L30: 
L31: We seek to break the barriers of traditional cancer treatment. Through collaboration with colleagues and research scientists, we want to offer the most effective cancer treatment for canine B cell lymphoma.
L32: ## Why We Do It
L33: 
L34: Canine B cell lymphoma is a very prevalent cancer in dogs of all breeds. It behaves much like non-Hodgkin lymphoma in humans and much of the research has taken place with dogs. Aurelius Biotherapeutics is utilizing this information and applying it to canine lymphoma treatment.
L35: ## Canine Lymphoma Treatment
L36: 
L37: For the past decade, our team has concentrated on the treatment of canine B cell lymphoma using adoptive transfer of T cells, commonly referred to as ACT. Our sole focus is to deliver safe and effective adoptive T cell immunotherapy in the fight against cancer. By using the patients own T cells, we can enhance the immune system so it can recognize and fight the cancer cells more effectively.
L38: ## What is T cell Therapy?
L39: 
L40: Cells from the patient's own immune system, T lymphocytes, are collected, cultured and activated to be tumor-cell specific. Once their numbers are maximally expanded, they are infused back in to the patient.  By recruiting the immune system we hope to provide another way to fight the cancer cells
L41: 
L42: 【12†Image: process of t cell therapy in treating lymphoma in dogs】
L43: ## T Cell Therapies
L44: Lately, immunotherapy treatment that uses the patients’ immune cells has grown in importance.  Adoptive transfer of T cells provides a novel approach in the fight against cancer. T cells are removed from the blood stream and those cells that are specifically fighting the cancer are selected and expanded. Recently, Novartis has won FDA approval for a unique form of T cell therapy using CAR T therapy.
L45: CAR T cell therapy refers to a process using the patients’ T cells which are selected and genetically modified to identify the tumor antigen more effectively. Aurelius Biotherapeutics uses another type of immunotherapy that doesn't genetically modify the T cells. By growing the lymphocytes with antigens from the tumor, we reactivate the T cells in their fight against the cancer cells.

L1: ## Doubling of survival chances in dogs with bladder cancer due to vaccine
L2: 
L3: 【0†Image: image】
L4: 
L5: Benno Therapeutics – Advancing Cancer Care for Dogs
L6: 
L7: Cancer is one of the most common and devastating diseases in companion animals. An estimated one in four dogs will develop cancer during their lifetime, with risk increasing significantly in dogs over the age of six. Despite this high prevalence, treatment options often remain limited, burdensome, or ineffective, especially for aggressive tumor types.
L8: Benno Therapeutics is dedicated to changing this. We are developing a new class of immunotherapies based on the iBOOST platform, originally created at Amsterdam UMC, to provide safer and more effective cancer treatments for dogs.
L9: 
L10: A Novel Approach: Targeting Tumor Blood Vessels, Not the Tumor
L11: 
L12: Traditional cancer treatments focus on destroying tumor cells directly. However, cancer cells mutate rapidly, often developing resistance to therapy. Benno Therapeutics takes a fundamentally different approach:
L13: We target the genetically stable blood vessels that tumors need to survive and grow.
L14: 
L15: Our lead candidate, BTX001, is a therapeutic vaccine designed to train the immune system to attack tumor-associated blood vessels. It does this by inducing antibodies against externalized vimentin (eVim)—a self-protein that becomes exposed on the surface of activated endothelial cells in tumor vasculature, but not on healthy tissues.
L16: To break immune tolerance, eVim is fused to a foreign carrier. This allows the vaccinated dog to generate strong antibody responses that:
L17: 
L18:   * Destroy tumor blood vessels
L19:   * Suppress tumor growth
L20:   * Limit metastatic spread
L21: 
L22: Importantly, extensive safety data show that this targeted approach is very safe, making BTX001 a promising therapeutic option for many cancer types.
L23: 
L24: 
L25: 
L26: Lead Indication: Canine Bladder Cancer
L27: Canine bladder cancer is a severe and life-threatening disease with no approved veterinary treatments. Current care typically relies on COX-2 inhibitors, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy, all of which have limited efficacy and can cause significant side effects. Chemotherapy also poses risks to owners due to the handling of toxic agents.
L28: 
L29: In an exploratory study in pet dogs, BTX001 demonstrated:
L30:   * An excellent safety profile
L31:   * A significantly improved survival rate compared with traditional treatments
L32: 
L33: Because BTX001 works by targeting tumor vasculature, a universal feature of solid tumors, it has the potential to benefit dogs with multiple cancer types, not just bladder cancer.
L34: 
L35: 
L36: 
L37: Promising Results in Hemangiosarcoma
L38: Visceral hemangiosarcoma is one of the most aggressive canine cancers. Because the disease progresses rapidly, vaccination alone does not allow enough time to build protective antibody levels. Instead, BTX001 was evaluated in combination with doxorubicin (DOX).
L39: 
L40: In a recently published prospective study, dogs receiving BTX001 + DOX achieved:
L41:   * Increased median survival from 136 to 235 days
L42:   * Significantly improved 1-year restricted mean survival
L43:   * A 1-year survival rate of 44%, compared with 14% in DOX-only controls
L44:   * No added toxicity from the vaccine
L45: 
L46: These results highlight the flexibility of the platform BTX001 can be used alone for slower-progressing tumors, or alongside chemotherapy when needed.
L47: 
L48: 
L49: 
L50: Expanding into Other Cancers: Osteosarcoma
L51: Osteosarcoma is an aggressive bone cancer where survival after amputation alone averages around 136 days, and without surgery only 1–3 months a  study in patient dogs receiving amputation plus BTX001 is ongoing.
L52: 
L53: A Broad Platform for Multiple Tumor Types
L54: 
L55: Benno Therapeutics’ strategy is based on a simple but powerful principle:
L56: One mechanism, multiple cancers.
L57: Because tumor blood vessels share the same biological features across cancer types, BTX001 may offer benefit across a wide spectrum of canine tumors. Ongoing and planned studies aim to further demonstrate this “single product, multiple cancers” potential.
L58:

L133: ElenaVet work?
L134: ### Why does your pet have a cancer?
L135: 
L136: Both pets and humans have pre-cancer and even cancer cells, but these bad cells can do no harm unless the tissue surrounding them allows the formation of primary tumors and the potential for metastasis.
L137: 
L138: Read more
L139: Often, pre-cancer cells can form tumors when a surrounding tissue is in a state of chronic inflammation. Additionally, tumors use chronic inflammation within the tumor to suppress the body’s natural anticancer immune response to resist treatments. Administering ElenaVet reduces chronic inflammation. This means it has excellent anti-cancer potency and synergizes well with other anti-cancer therapies.
L140: 
L141: Less
L142: A tumor is not a bag full of cancer cells. Cancer cells cannot survive without the support of tumor stroma cells. ElenaVet alters tumor stroma making it less supportive for cancer cells. For example, a tumor prognosis is correlated with an expression of a protein called α-SMA. Our product reduced the tumor risk modulating α-SMA ‘s expression level. 【12†Image†veterinary.curelaboncology.com】

L203: Cells and tissues “scream for help” — sending out pro-inflammatory cytokines. When the danger is over, anti-inflammatory cytokines calm the tissue down.
